- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: Every step after the first finds its own PR, does a no-op self-merge, and emits the wrong "older PR can be closed" message. Closing it forces a §21.A reset and a new draft PR.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: The defect propagates to every consumer repo on the next `@stable` sync.

  WHY: It does not fail.

  WHY: It does not fail; the scope is bounded.

- TASK_GAP (covered, NIT, confidence 5): Requirement: the first log commit opens one draft PR titled `chore: activation log updates`. Expected change site: the same bullet. Evidence: covered at line 59.

Expected change site: test_one_session_keeps_its_log_updates_in_one_pull_request. Evidence: lines 211-244 cover the literal text, but no test asserts the self-match exclusion.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The earlier-session log-PR detection criterion does not exclude the session's own log PR (also line 55, and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md lines 62 and 66), so a resumed invocation self-matches.
  WHY: The session merges its own branch (a no-op) and tells the operator the "older PR can be closed". If the operator closes it, the next log commit hits the §21.A restart and opens a second draft PR. tests/test_deploy_activate_command.py:226-236 pins the current wording.
